name: Mīr Sayyid Sharīf ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Jurjānī
summary: Ḥanafī scholar of Shiraz whose Persian primers Naḥw-i Mīr and Ṣarf-i Mīr open the grammar of the Indian and Central Asian madrasas.
bio: Al-Sayyid al-Sharīf was born near Astarābād in 740/1340 and died in Shiraz in 816/1413. He wrote some fifty works in Arabic and Persian, including glosses on the great books of balāgha, logic and kalām.
His two short Persian primers, Naḥw-i Mīr on syntax and Ṣarf-i Mīr on inflection, became the first grammar books of countless students in the Indian subcontinent and Central Asia.
